title: Career coaching & guidance in English, in Italy – Blooming
description: Career guidance with a psychologist who has worked in HR for over ten years and knows the Italian job market. Online, in English. Free first meeting.

data.title: Finding your direction at work, in the life you're building here.

p.t: One-to-one career coaching in English with a psychologist who has worked in HR for over ten years. For anyone who has moved to Italy, or is about to, and wants work that fits the rest of their life. Sessions are online, by video call.

data.title: Where you might be starting from.

items.title: Applications go nowhere, and everyone says it's who you know

p.t: You've sent CV after CV and can't even get an interview. A CV written for another job market can come across very differently to a recruiter here, and contacts matter when you have almost none yet.

items.title: Your qualifications and experience don't seem to count

p.t: Years of work and a degree that opened doors at home now seem to carry little weight. Getting a qualification formally recognised is a separate process, and it takes time.

items.title: You followed your partner, and your own career went on hold

p.t: The move made sense for both of you. Now your partner has a job to go to and you're the one rebuilding from scratch, often in a language you're still learning. How you spend your days affects everything else, at home as well as at work.

items.title: You're moving soon and want a plan before you arrive

p.t: You'd rather know what's realistic before you land: which roles are open to you, how much Italian they need, and what to prepare while you're still abroad.

items.title: You have a job, but it isn't going anywhere

p.t: You've settled in, the work is fine, and there's no obvious next step. You may be wondering whether to push for more where you are, change field, or leave Italy altogether.
If this feels harder than you expected, you're not alone: 42% of expats in Italy rate the local job market negatively.

data.title: It starts with your situation, not with your CV.

p.t: Career coaching is a series of one-to-one video sessions. It's practical work on your career, led by a psychologist, and it isn't therapy. What you do in the sessions depends on where you're starting from.

The psychologist starts by looking at your skills and experience and what you want from work. Then come the things you have to plan around, such as how much Italian you speak, family, a visa or where you'd like to live. Moving country changes your working life and your home life at the same time, so a career plan that leaves one of them out rarely holds up for long.

items.title: Then a realistic look at what's open to you

p.t: An ad that asks for "fluent Italian" doesn't always mean it. Your psychologist has spent years on the other side of job ads, so she can help you tell a hard requirement from a wish list, and say plainly how much Italian the roles you want are likely to need. From there you compare the options that are realistically open, and decide whether a course or a new qualification would actually change your chances.

data.title: A psychologist who is also an HR professional.

people.name: Career coaching & guidance

p.t: Career coaching is led by a psychologist, registered with the Italian Order of Psychologists since 2014, whose entry in the Order's register states that she offers sessions in English. She has worked in HR for over ten years, across recruitment, development, training and change management, and knows the Italian job market. She also has international academic and professional experience.

That combination shapes the sessions. When she reads your CV or runs a mock interview, she draws on years of HR work, recruitment included. As a psychologist, she can also work with what a career change does to your confidence and your days, alongside the practical steps.
